title: Police still serve political interests, says Shujan's Badiul Alam
excerpt: At Shujan's 24th anniversary in Narayanganj, the citizens' group called for an independent, accountable police force.

image.credit: P.K. Niyogi / Wikimedia Commons, public domain

content:
Law enforcement agencies still follow old practices, including political patronage, Badiul Alam Majumdar, secretary of the citizens' group Shushashoner Jonno Nagorik (Shujan), said in Narayanganj on Saturday, 14 November, The Business Standard reported.

He spoke at a discussion on a drug-free and violence-free Narayanganj, held at the Ali Ahmed Chunka City Library and Auditorium to mark Shujan's 24th anniversary. Additional Superintendent of Police Tarek Al Mehedi and local civic, media and party leaders also took part.

What he said

  • Police should stop trying to please political leaders and work independently, with integrity and respect for citizens' rights.
  • The administration appears sincere about tackling drugs and crime, but political patronage of criminals continues "from different quarters", including within law enforcement, according to the report.
  • Police cannot solve these problems alone, and citizens need to move from discussion to action.

He recalled Narayanganj's history of high-profile killings, including the "seven murders" case and the killing of teenager Taqi. The report gives his remarks mostly in paraphrase, and does not say what the police officer or other speakers said.

Why it matters

Police reform was a central demand after the 2024 uprising. Rights groups, legal aid NGOs and local civic platforms that document abuses or support victims depend on police that act independently. Shujan's message is that the reform agenda has not yet changed practice on the ground.

What to watch

Progress on police reform proposals in Parliament, and whether local citizens' committees like Shujan's gain a formal role in community safety.

Sources

  • Law enforcers continuing past practices: Badiul Alam Majumdar, The Business Standard, 15 November 2026
